IncBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: surge of 502/504 + connection resets observed for services behind ALB-euc1b-targets — 5xx rate up 18% in last 2m
alice (on-call): paging oncall, I’m looking. do we have a blast radius?
bob (ingress): seeing Envoy upstream_conn_reset and 502s from pods in euc1b-azb. 3/12 pods showing reset spikes.
carla (netops): confirmed NLB metrics show increased target connection errors in euc1b. DNS for some subnets also reports timeouts.
alice (on-call): @bob can you run /kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=envoy -o wide and tail logs for the failing pods?
bob (ingress): running
```
kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=envoy -o wide
kubectl logs -n ingress envoy-27f8 -c envoy --since=5m | grep upstream_conn_reset || true
```

bob (ingress): envoy-27f8 and envoy-2a4c have repeated "connection reset by peer" entries and OOM killer not present. CPU and sockets look normal.
alice (on-call): @carla any routing changes or infra events in euc1b?
carla (netops): infra shows an AZ network fabric flapping for euc1b-azb since 1820012280. Fabric retries hit our infra-lb in that AZ, causing upstream resets from targets behind that AZ. AWS health shows transient ENI detach events.
tim (platform): rolling restart of envoy pods in that AZ might help, but we should fail traffic away from the AZ first. proposing: 1) mark unhealthy targets in ALB target group for euc1b-azb 2) increase weight to euc1a & euc1c 3) drain / restart envoy in azb
alice (on-call): agreed. @sre-bot please create incident channel and run the runbook for ALB target failover.
sre-bot: created incident channel #incident-1820012345, incident id INC-18200. Runbook step: set target group health to draining for azb targets.
carla (netops): doing ALB target deregister for target-group tg-abc123: deregistering targets in euc1b-azb now.
carla (netops): deregistration started, health checks moving to draining -> expected failover within 30s.
bob (ingress): starting rolling restart of envoy in euc1b: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/ingress-envoy -n ingress --field-selector spec.nodeName=euc1b-*`
alice (on-call): also temp-scaling: bump ingress replicas in euc1a/c to absorb traffic surge.
tim (platform): scaling ingress horizontally now: scaled from 6->12 across healthy AZs.
carla (netops): ALB targets in azb now showing 0 healthy. Traffic shifted to a/c. NLB metrics show healthy.
bob (ingress): after restart, envoy logs stop showing upstream_conn_reset for restarted pods. connection reset metric down ~80% in the restarted subset.
alice (on-call): monitoring customer impact — SLO dashboards show error rate across all customers back to baseline except a small subset pinned to azb IP ranges.
pagerduty: acked by alice (on-call) 1820012350
carla (netops): note: DNS TTL for internal load-balancer VIPs is 60s; some clients pinned to earlier sockets still hitting azb until connection churn. expect residual 5xx for up to 2 minutes.
alice (on-call): customer-facing: support-notify runbook queued. @tim please prepare a short message: impact, mitigation, ETA to full recovery.
tim (platform): draft: "We experienced intermittent 5xx errors for services routed via euc1b due to an AZ network fabric instability. Traffic has been re-routed and ingress controllers restarted; most traffic is healthy. We expect residual errors to subside within 5-10 minutes. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident summary."
alice (on-call): send when ready.
bob (ingress): adding firewall/NACL check: no recent changes. problem appears infra-level.
carla (netops): opened AWS support ticket 2026-ECU-4921 referencing ENI detaches in euc1b-azb for customers running ENI-based routing.
sre-bot: incident status -> mitigation: reroute + restarts completed at 1820012420.
alice (on-call): verifying metrics: 5xx spike dropped from 18% -> 1.6% overall. p50 latency normal. p95 improved.
tim (platform): customer list for potential impact: commerce-prod, billing-api, partner-ingest (all with endpoints in euc1b). recommend targeted postmortem with those owners.
alice (on-call): tagging owners: @bob FYI notify commerce-prod on expected brief window of errors and ops actions.
bob (ingress): notified commerce-prod and billing-api, sent logs and timeline.
carla (netops): AWS reports transient fabric flaps tied to a vendor switch in euc1b-azb, they claim ongoing remediation. we should treat this as external root cause.
alice (on-call): next steps: 1) leave ALB targets deregistered for azb until AWS fully stabilizes 2) schedule rollout of NLB health-check tuning to detect similar ENI detach faster 3) postmortem with timelines and customer impact 4) follow-up with AWS support.
alice (on-call): opening a postmortem doc in confluence: /confluence/INC-18200-postmortem (placeholder). please add timelines and command output.
bob (ingress): uploading logs to s3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-18200/envoy-logs.tar.gz
carla (netops): closing mitigation window, continue monitoring for 30m.
alice (on-call): incident status -> monitoring. will update channel when we switch to resolved. great job team, :thumbsup:
inc closing note (alice): incident resolved at 1820012598. root cause: AZ network fabric instability causing ENI detach and upstream_conn_reset on envoy targets; mitigation: ALB target deregistration, ingress restarts, traffic redistribution. follow-ups: postmortem + AWS remediation tracking.
